message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI Command

```bash
# Replace placeholders:
#   PROJECT_ID – your GCP project ID
#   ZONE       – e.g., us-central1-a
#   INSTANCE   – a unique name for the VM

gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE \
    --project=$PROJECT_ID \
    --zone=$ZONE \
    --machine-type=e2-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory allocation. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--image-project` & `--image-family` | Pulls Ubuntu 20.04 LTS from the official Ubuntu image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | Size & performance of the boot disk. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Terminates the instance if the host machine is rebooted (common for GPU nodes). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Automatically restarts the instance if it crashes. |

> **Tip:**  
> - Ensure the **Compute Engine API** is enabled for your project.  
> - Billing must be active; GPU instances incur additional charges.  
> - You might need to add the **NVIDIA GPU driver** installation step in a startup script (`startup.sh`) so the GPU is ready after boot.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a minimal payload you’d POST to:

```
https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

```json
{
  "name": "{INSTANCE}",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/e2-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

> **Notes:**
> - Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{INSTANCE}` with your actual values.  
> - The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver automatically. Adjust the driver version if needed.  
> - Make sure you have OAuth 2.0 credentials with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.

---

### Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Enable APIs** – Compute Engine API + Cloud Resource Manager API.  
2. **Billing** – Ensure your project has an active billing account.  
3. **Permissions** – Your service account or user must have `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`.  
4. **GPU Quota** – Verify you have enough GPU quota in the selected zone.  

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh $USER@$EXTERNAL_IP
nvidia-smi
```

That should show the RTX A6000 GPU and its driver status. Happy computing!
